under your service. Please validate that the API has been identified

does not change or limit your network calls.

[Webium] Use the user profile for the autoplay policy

DetermineWebContentsAutoplayPolicy() uses the profile of the
WebContents, while the rest of its WebPreferences use its user profile,
see GetProfileForWebPreferences(). They are the same, except for a
WebContents in TopChromeWebUIProfile, which hosts the Top Chrome WebUIs
of the windows of all profiles with kTopChromeWebUISharedRenderer.
That profile has no HostContentSettingsMap, so computing the
WebPreferences of the WebUI toolbar (crrev.com/c/8567399) in it crashes
with media::kAutoplayDisableSettings.

DetermineWebContentsAutoplayPolicy() now uses the user profile too.

[crubit] Add `root_namespaces` parameter to `rust_api_from_cpp`.

Before this CL, Rust code had to use the full C++ namespace path to
refer to items from `rust_api_from_cpp` bindings (e.g.
`base_rs_api::base::Foo`).

After this CL, the new `root_namespaces` parameter re-exports items of
the specified C++ namespaces at the root of the generated crate (e.g.
`base_rs_api::Foo`).  The parameter maps to the
`--reexported_namespaces` flag of `rs_bindings_from_cc`.

`base_rs_api`, the first examples in `rust_api_from_cpp.md`, and the
matching test targets now use `root_namespaces`.  This hopefully
spreads awareness of this commonly useful attribute.

[gardener] Suppress flaky DIP navigate-across-policies WPT on x64 Mac

navigate-across-policies.tentative.https.html came in with the wpt
import in https://crrev.com/c/8667146. On x64 Mac builders passing
runs take 57 to 59 s against the 60 s long timeout, and
mac15-x64-rel-tests #22856 timed out on all 10 runs. Arm64 Mac, Linux,
and Windows finish in 3 to 7 s.

Mark it [ Pass Timeout ] on Mac13, Mac14, and Mac15, next to
back-forward-cache.tentative.https.html, which has the same problem.

Traverse children of kept SVG <use> in StripSvgUseNonLocalHrefs()

StripSvgUseNonLocalHrefs() previously returned `true` unconditionally
after inspecting an SVGUseElement, even when the element had a local
`href` and remained in the fragment. That early return skipped
traversing its descendant nodes, allowing nested `<use>` elements with
non-local or `data:` `href` attributes to survive paste sanitization
when the serializer preserved unrendered descendants (e.g., inside
`<select>` or with `display: contents`).

Move `return true;` inside the removal branch so that
StripSvgUseNonLocalHrefs() continues traversing children of kept
`<use>` elements and returns `true` only when it actually removes at
least one `<use>` element, matching its documentation comment.

[Views] Fix UAF when a menu is closed while MenuModelAdapter rebuilds it

MenuModelAdapter::BuildMenu() rebuilds a showing menu in place. If the
menu is closed and its MenuRunner released while BuildMenu() is on the
stack, the MenuItemView tree (owned by MenuRunnerImpl) and the
MenuModelAdapter (owned by MenuRunnerImplAdapter) are destroyed
synchronously. BuildMenu() then keeps using the freed items, submenu
and adapter, and deletes the removed items a second time.

This can be triggered through EditableCombobox, which rebuilds its
dropdown on every keystroke. Each inserted item fires an accessibility
event, and an assistive technology moving focus in response closes the
menu:

  EditableCombobox::ContentsChanged
  -> MenuModelAdapter::BuildMenu
  -> MenuItemView::AddMenuItemAt
  -> MenuItemView::UpdateAccessibleName  // sync a11y event
  -> EditableCombobox::OnViewBlurred     // AT moved focus
  -> EditableCombobox::CloseMenu
  -> MenuRunnerImplAdapter::Release      // deletes MenuModelAdapter
  -> MenuRunnerImpl::Release
  -> MenuController::Cancel              // deletes MenuItemView tree

Fix by holding a MenuController::ScopedDeletionGuard in BuildMenu()
while the menu is showing, so that destruction of the controller, the
MenuRunnerImpl and the menu is deferred until the rebuild is done. To
also keep the MenuModelAdapter alive, MenuRunnerImplAdapter::Release()
now hands it to the MenuRunnerImpl instead of deleting it.

This CL does not address crbug.com/562001435, which is a different
use-after-free.

re-enables PageLoadAndTabSwitchTriggersPrewarm:

Webium: add `NewWindowCreationSource::kNavigation`

Previously, normal browser windows created during navigation paths and
`ScopedTabbedBrowserDisplayer` did not set a window creation source on
`InitialWebUIWindowMetricsManager`.

This CL:
- Adds `NewWindowCreationSource::kNavigation` (`.Navigation`) and sets
  it in `CreateNormalBrowserForNavigation()` (`browser_navigator.cc`)
  and `CreateNormalBrowserWindow()` (`navigation_capturing_process.cc`).
- Sets `NewWindowCreationSource::kNewEmptyWindow` in
  `ScopedTabbedBrowserDisplayer` (`scoped_tabbed_browser_displayer.cc`)
  when opening an empty window because the profile has none.

Fix dangling raw_ptr in DoesCSPDisallowRemoteCode

Declare `csp_parser` before the `DirectiveMapping` stack variables so
that `csp_parser` outlives the `raw_ptr<const CSPParser::Directive>`
fields pointing into `csp_parser.directives()`, and remove the
`DanglingUntriaged` annotation.

Also convert `DirectiveMapping` into an aggregate initialized with
designated initializers and remove unused includes from
`csp_validator.cc`.

[base] Re-enable `ProcessMetricsTest.GetNumberOfThreads` on Linux

Re-enable `ProcessMetricsTest.GetNumberOfThreads` in `base_unittests` on
Linux and ChromeOS by waiting for `/proc/<pid>/stat` thread count
updates.

`ProcessMetricsTest.GetNumberOfThreads` was disabled on Linux builders
in https://crrev.com/288722 (tracked in https://crbug.com/396455) due to
flakiness.

The test verifies that `GetNumberOfThreads()` reports an accurate thread
count as threads are added and removed. However, in Linux NPTL,
`pthread_join()` returns as soon as the exiting thread clears its child
TID futex during `exit_mm()`, before the kernel completes
`release_task()` and decrements `signal->nr_threads`. Consequently,
querying `GetNumberOfThreads()` immediately upon thread start or join
can observe a slight lag in `/proc/<pid>/stat` updates (as documented in
`sandbox/linux/services/thread_helpers.cc`).

This CL introduces `WaitForNumberOfThreads()` to poll with a timeout
until the expected thread count is reflected in `/proc`, eliminating the
kernel race condition and re-enabling the test in `base_unittests`.

Part of http://go/arthurmilchior-fix-all-test-skill-chrome for AI week.

Fix selected tab contrast in Windows high contrast mode

Multi-selected inactive tabs use the active foreground but retain a
Material selected background. In the Windows Aquatic theme, this renders
dark highlight text on a dark background.

Use native highlight backgrounds for selected tabs in both window
activation and hover states, use native highlight text for inactive
windows.

[Views] Re-enable TextareaTest.MoveUpDownAndModifySelection on Mac

`TextareaTest.MoveUpDownAndModifySelection` was disabled on macOS when
`Textarea` was initially introduced in https://crrev.com/c/2519764 due
to `RenderText::GetCursorBounds` miscomputing multiline cursor positions
when moving across lines.

The underlying multiline cursor bounds and newline glyph width bugs in
`RenderText` were subsequently fixed in https://crrev.com/c/2613424 and
https://crrev.com/c/3017262. Re-enable the test on macOS.

Part of http://go/arthurmilchior-fix-all-test-skill-chrome for AI week.

[Reading Mode] Set Readability distillation state in the renderer.

Previously, since Readability distillations were initiated by the
browser process, ReadAnythingUntrustedPageHandler had to send
distillation state updates to the renderer over Mojo via
OnReadabilityDistillationStateChanged(). With
kReadAnythingDistillerRefactor, Readability distillations are initiated
in the renderer and return via the request callback, so we can manage
ReadAnythingDistillationState entirely in the renderer (avoiding
cross-pipe ordering races with the reply). This matches Screen2x
behavior.

This CL:
- Sets kDistillationInProgress in ProcessModelUpdates() when starting a
  Readability re-distillation (matching OnActiveAXTreeIDChanged()).
- Sets kDistillationWithContent in UpdateContent() when Readability
  returns content, and leaves empty/ineligible fallbacks to Screen2x.
- Skips OnReadabilityDistillationStateChanged() in
  ReadAnythingUntrustedPageHandler when kReadAnythingDistillerRefactor
  is enabled.

[X11] End all touch sequences that a grabbed move loop ends

X11WholeScreenMoveLoop consumes touch releases while a data drag or tab
drag runs, and X11Window dispatched a touch cancel for each one once
the loop returned. Two cases were missed, so aura::Env kept reporting
those touches as held:

- The cancel was sent to the X11Window for the XI2 event window of the
  consumed release. While the loop holds its own pointer grab, that
  window is the loop's private input window, which is not an
  X11Window, so no cancel was dispatched.
- Releasing the loop's pointer grab ends every touch sequence that is
  still active (e.g. when the loop ends on Escape, a mouse click, or
  the release of another finger), and the X server reports their end
  relative to the loop's input window, which no X11Window handles.

X11WindowManager now tracks the touch sequences dispatched to each
X11Window that have not ended. After a move loop, X11Window cancels the
consumed sequences on the windows they were dispatched to, regardless
of the event window of the release. If the loop grabbed the pointer
itself, it cancels all sequences that are still active. A loop that
did not grab the pointer (e.g. a tab drag whose window has capture)
still leaves sequences that are down alone, so a tab drag that
re-attaches to a tab strip with the finger still down is unaffected.

Revert "[ContextualTasks] Redirect standalone WebUI to AIM"

This reverts commit f204bf5628d52788ffb98b9e224593abac88ae4e.

Reason for revert: Revert of [ContextualTasks] Redirect standalone
WebUI to AIM due to breaking GuestUtilBrowserTest.OnGuestAdded_NonGlic
on linux-chromeos-chrome

Failure Link: https://ci.chromium.org/b/8666657350562520609

Original change's description:
> [ContextualTasks] Redirect standalone WebUI to AIM
>
> When `kContextualTasks` is disabled and only `kContextualTasksSidePanel`
> is enabled, signed-in users still satisfy general eligibility checks,
> allowing direct standalone tab navigations to load an inactive full-tab
> WebUI. Redirecting non-side-panel WebUI navigations in
> `HandleNavigationImpl` routes standalone tabs to AI Mode (AIM) while
> leaving post-rearchitecture routing untouched, where the standalone root
> WebUI does not exist.
>
> When `kContextualTasks` is enabled, standalone WebUI navigations
> continue directly to `chrome://contextual-tasks`. Diagnostic pages
> under `/internals`, WebUI test harness paths, and side-panel web
> contents remain exempt from redirection.
>

Avoid redundant map lookup in PreconnectManagerImpl::Start

In PreconnectManagerImpl::Start, preresolve_info_.find(url) was called
twice if the URL already existed in the map (once in the if condition
and again in the else branch).

Store the iterator from the initial lookup and reuse it in the else
branch to avoid the second map lookup.

Revert "[glic] Stop treating a client waiting for sign-in as a load failure"

This reverts commit 1cbc950af9a787a947fe4d2c7806c81bd73d5851.

Reason for revert: Revert 1cbc950af9a787a947fe4d2c7806c81bd73d5851 due
to test regression in
GlicInvokeBrowserTest.LiveModeForceSidePanelTextModeWithFloatingTargetIsInvalid
on linux-chromeos-chrome

Failure Link: https://ci.chromium.org/b/8666664621385627745

Original change's description:
> [glic] Stop treating a client waiting for sign-in as a load failure
>
> When the web client stops on the sign-in panel, glic_app_controller.ts
> reports it as a client load failure (hasClientLoadFailed(kSignIn)), so
> WaitForClientReadyTask ended the invocation with kClientLoadError and
> MapInvokeErrorToCuiOutcome recorded FAILED. Since CUI 1 is resolved from
> the invocation (crrev.com/c/8564501) that also made
> Glic.CUI.WindowEntryPointInvocation.Outcome count sign-in as FAILED,
> where before M158 the tracker never resolved on kSignIn and recorded the
> close that followed as ABANDONED. On Canary M158 that is ~9% of the CUI 1
> FAILED bucket.
>
> A client waiting for the user to sign in has not failed: it reloads and
> becomes ready once they do. What the invocation should do depends on
> what it needs (SignInBehavior):
>
> - An invocation that only shows the panel is done once the panel shows
>   what it should, and the sign-in panel is that: WaitForClientReadyTask
>   completes and the invocation succeeds.
> - An invocation that needs the client (requires_client_invoke) can do
>   nothing before the user signs in, so the task keeps waiting; the client
>   reloads and becomes ready when they do. If they have not by the
>   timeout, GlicInvokeHandler::OnTimeout() ends it with the new
>   GlicInvokeError::kSignInRequired (27) rather than kTimeout, which
>   MapInvokeErrorToCuiOutcome maps to GlicCuiOutcome::kAbandoned: nothing
>   the product did ran late.
>
> Both outcomes come from the invocation, so UMA CUI 1 and the structured
> InvokeTerminated keep agreeing.
>
> Host keeps the reason of the current failure
> (client_load_error_reason()): both hosts report the cause through
> ClientLoadErrorOccurred() before the failure bit that puts the client
> into kError, and the reason is cleared whenever the failure is withdrawn
> (reload, retry on show) or the client becomes ready, so it never
> describes an earlier load. A sign-in reached with the panel hidden has no
> reported cause and stays kClientLoadError.
>
> Bug: b:572879675

Allow reinvoking the Lens overlay from the contextual tasks composebox

Permits reinvoking the Lens overlay when the invocation source is the
Contextual Tasks composebox. Additionally, updates the query flow router
to check that the search controller is not off rather than checking if
the overlay is showing before scheduling the overlay to close on a
contextual text query.

Previously, headless contextual text queries (like Omnibox contextual
suggestions) started a Lens session without showing the overlay,
stranding the controller in an initializing state when gating cleanup on
`IsOverlayShowing()`. Closing any non-off session resets state after
handoff, while allowing `kContextualTasksComposebox` reinvocation
supports composebox Lens clicks during active sessions.

Mac: Fix pasteboard observation crash after main thread shutdown

The _CFPasteboardCache swizzle installed by
RegisterPasteboardChangedCallback() is never removed, and since r1625756
it calls SingleThreadTaskRunner::GetMainThreadDefault() on an internal
CFPasteboard dispatch queue. At browser shutdown the main thread's
default task runner handle is destroyed before the process exits, so a
pasteboard change in another app during that window hits the CHECK in
GetMainThreadDefault().

Capture the main thread's task runner at registration and post to it
from the swizzled method instead. After the main thread's task runner
shuts down, posted tasks are dropped.

[aw][hp] Only create HeapProfilerController in WebView if collection enabled

When features::kWebViewMemoryProfilingClient is enabled,
AwMainDelegate::InitializeMemorySystem created a HeapProfilerController
during startup on the UI thread for every session. Even though 99.9% of
Stable sessions are not selected for profiling (probability = 0.001),
all of them paid for the controller's construction leading to 9ms P95
regression in WebView's startup time.

This CL changes the behaviour such that SetProfilingParameters, and
consequently heap_profiler_controller construction, is only set when
actual collection is enabled.

Chrome behaviour is unchanged: it still always creates a controller,
which makes the same decision as before. Follow-up cl to update the
logic to apply to all platforms instead of just WebView.

[DCSI] Implement SupportsAccess for WrappedSkImageBacking

When features::kUseDynamicBackingAllocations is enabled,
CompoundImageBacking::GetOrAllocateBacking() queries
SharedImageBacking::SupportsAccess(stream, params) on existing elements
to determine whether an existing backing can serve a requested
SharedImageAccessStream or whether a new backing needs to be dynamically
allocated.

Previously, WrappedSkImageBacking did not override SupportsAccess(),
defaulting to returning true for all streams, and
WrappedSkImageBackingFactory::IsSupportedForAccessStream() also
unconditionally returned true when !use_graphite_. As a result, when a
SharedImage was initially backed by WrappedSkImageBacking under Ganesh
and a client later requested a non-Skia representation (such as
ProduceGLTexture*, ProduceVideo, or ProduceDawn), CompoundImageBacking
selected the existing WrappedSkImageBacking instead of dynamically
allocating a compatible backing, causing representation creation to
fail.

Implement WrappedSkImageBacking::CheckSupportForAccessStream() and
WrappedSkImageBacking::SupportsAccess() to only support kSkia with a
Ganesh SharedContextState when kUseDynamicBackingAllocations is enabled,
and delegate to CheckSupportForAccessStream() in
WrappedSkImageBackingFactory::IsSupportedForAccessStream(). Also use
ui::ScopedMakeCurrent in WrappedSkImageBacking::UploadFromMemory() and
ReadbackToMemory() so that the backing's SharedContextState is made
current and any previously current GL context is restored afterward.

[MediaCapture] Re-enable LoopsAllMediaAccessHandlers unit test

Re-enable
`MediaCaptureDevicesDispatcherTest.LoopsAllMediaAccessHandlers` after
fixing a state corruption issue on the singleton dispatcher.

`MediaCaptureDevicesDispatcherTest.LoopsAllMediaAccessHandlers` was
added in https://crrev.com/c/2111931 to verify that
`MediaCaptureDevicesDispatcher::UpdateVideoScreenCaptureStatus` loops
through registered handlers to find one supporting the given stream
type. It was subsequently disabled across platforms in
https://crrev.com/c/2232325 due to https://crbug.com/1069045 because of
flaky crashes on the bots.

The test cleared `media_access_handlers_` directly on the singleton
`MediaCaptureDevicesDispatcher::GetInstance()`. This destroyed the
registered handlers for the lifetime of the process, leaving
`desktop_capture_access_handler_for_test_` as a dangling pointer and
polluting subsequent unit tests in the same process batch.

To fix this, preserve the original `media_access_handlers_` and
`desktop_capture_access_handler_for_test_` on the singleton and restore
them at test completion via `base::ScopedClosureRunner`.

Part of http://go/arthurmilchior-fix-all-test-skill-chrome for AI week.

Revert "Reland "Use -mcmodel=medium for ELF x64 sanitizer builds""

This reverts commit 1e1b6dc72eed50c5b7f545b8041240259fa4958c.

Reason for revert: Suspects making Linux CFI compile time out. With
-mcmodel=medium, the ThinLTO CFI links of browser_tests, unit_tests and
components_unittests do not finish within the 5h task timeout (Linux CFI
[#33135](https://ci.chromium.org/b/8666690152521184721) and [#33136](
https://ci.chromium.org/b/8666671143524473889); 3 LINK steps still
running after about 4h37m). The original CL caused the same timeout in
[#33130](https://ci.chromium.org/b/8666754949700780193), and the first
build after its revert (#33131) linked the same targets in 39 to 78
minutes. Linux CFI sets use_cfi_diag, so using_sanitizer is true and the
flag applies there.

Bug: 577661175

Failure Link: https://ci.chromium.org/p/chromium/builders/ci/Linux%20CFI/b8666690152521184721

Original change's description:
> Reland "Use -mcmodel=medium for ELF x64 sanitizer builds"
>
> This is a reland of commit 4714cff9778c641f4d0ef4ce958a9142a8488b2c
>
> Excluded `is_ubsan_security` builds from `-mcmodel=medium` because
> `-fsanitize=function` is only supported with `-mcmodel=small`.
>
> Original change's description:
> > Use -mcmodel=medium for ELF x64 sanitizer builds
> >
> > Sanitizer instrumentation inflates data sections (.data, .bss, etc.),
> > making large binaries prone to exceeding the 2GiB displacement limit of
> > the default small code model and failing at link time with "relocation
> > R_X86_64_PC32 out of range".
> >
> > On Windows (PE/COFF) and macOS (Mach-O), the object formats do not
> > support large sections, so we only enable the flag for ELF targets.
> >

Mark Opaque XR framebuffers as incomplete on session end

Ensures that Opaque framebuffers created by WebXR are always marked
as incomplete at the end of an XR frame, even if the session ended
during the frame.

As an additional guard against accessing orphaned shared image
texture handles via an opaque framebuffer, ensure that the color
textures are detached from the framebuffer when the frame ends.

profile directory only if the profile directory is under the XDG config
directory (e.g. ~/.config), which is never the case for ChromeOS user
profiles (/home/chronos/u-<hash>). Use the profile path directly in
drive::util::GetCacheRootPath(), and remove chrome_paths_internal.h from
chrome/browser/ash/drive/DEPS.

login: Inject LoginDisplayHost dependencies into ShowLoginWizard()

ShowLoginWizard() reads local_state, metrics_service,
application_locale_storage, shared_url_loader_factory and
browser_policy_connector_ash from g_browser_process, to create the
LoginDisplayHost and, for local_state, for its own startup logic. Take
them as parameters from its callers instead, and remove its
TODO(crbug.com/403154552) block. Its remaining g_browser_process use,
TimeZoneResolverManager::UpdateTimezoneResolver(), is left for a
separate change with a TODO. The LoginDisplayHost may be created
asynchronously after a locale switch; the dependencies reach it through
ShowLoginWizardFinish() as before.

ChromeSessionManager::Initialize() already holds all five, so
StartLoginOobeSession() takes them from it, which keeps
chrome_session_manager.cc free of g_browser_process. SwitchWebUItoMojo()
keeps its signature for now and passes the g_browser_process values,
with a TODO; passing them from WizardController is left to a follow-up.
The three browser tests that call ShowLoginWizard() pass the
g_browser_process values.

The callers pass the same process-wide objects that ShowLoginWizard()
used to read, so this doesn't change behavior.

Dependency injection flow:
  ChromeBrowserMainPartsAsh::PostProfileInit
  +--> ChromeSessionManager::Initialize
       +--> StartLoginOobeSession
            +--> ShowLoginWizard
                 +--> TriggerShowLoginWizardFinish
                      +--> [OnLanguageSwitchedCallback]
                           +--> ShowLoginWizardFinish
                                +--> LoginDisplayHostMojo /
                                     LoginDisplayHostWebUI

  SwitchWebUItoMojo (g_browser_process, TODO)
  +--> ShowLoginWizard

TAG=agy

login: Pass ShowLoginWizard() dependencies to ShowLoginWizardFinish()

ShowLoginWizard() already reads local_state, metrics_service,
application_locale_storage, shared_url_loader_factory and
browser_policy_connector_ash from g_browser_process. Pass them down
through TriggerShowLoginWizardFinish() and OnLanguageSwitchedCallback()
to ShowLoginWizardFinish(), which constructs the LoginDisplayHost,
instead of reading them from g_browser_process again. This removes the
TODO(crbug.com/403154552) block in ShowLoginWizardFinish() and the
TODO(crbug.com/404133029) read in TriggerShowLoginWizardFinish().
ShowLoginWizardFinish() now moves the factory into the host it creates.

When a locale switch is needed, the dependencies are bound into the
locale_util::SwitchLanguage() callback. The getters return the same
process-wide objects, so this doesn't change behavior. The bound raw
pointers remain valid whenever OnLanguageSwitchedCallback() runs (on the
UI thread while the main RunLoop is running, before
BrowserProcessImpl::StartTearDown() destroys any of the dependencies),
and ShowLoginWizardFinish() returns early once shutdown has started.

Dependency injection flow:
  ShowLoginWizard
  +--> TriggerShowLoginWizardFinish
       +--> ShowLoginWizardFinish
       +--> OnLanguageSwitchedCallback (after a locale switch)
            +--> ShowLoginWizardFinish
                 +--> LoginDisplayHostMojo / LoginDisplayHostWebUI

TAG=agy

feature has been enabled by default, so remove the flag entry and the

non-multi-display tablet context in CompositorView).

feec3e707d83ddc14f625b42311934fc16a768c5 [ diff ] 
[iOS] Enable NetworkQualityEstimatorTest throughput and ECT tests

Re-enable NetworkQualityEstimatorTest.TestThroughputNoRequestOverlap
(disabled in crrev.com/c/2311116) and
NetworkQualityEstimatorTest.TestEffectiveConnectionTypeObserver
(disabled in crrev.com/c/2560253002) on iOS.

When these tests were disabled, they ran URLRequests against a local
EmbeddedTestServer using TestURLRequestContext and could flake in
net_unittests due to unisolated host resolution, race conditions in
initial observer notifications and async throughput window startup, and
overflow when computing throughput for near-zero-duration local
responses. Since then, those root causes have been fixed:
- crrev.com/c/734582 moved `add_default_platform_observations` into
  `NetworkQualityEstimatorParams` (preventing default observations from
  being added in the base constructor before the test disabled them) and
  drained the initial `AddEffectiveConnectionTypeObserver()` task with
  `RunUntilIdle()` in `TestEffectiveConnectionTypeObserver`.
- crrev.com/c/3353583 migrated `NetworkQualityEstimatorTest` from
  `TestURLRequestContext` to `CreateTestURLRequestContextBuilder()`,
  providing an isolated `MockCachingHostResolver` pre-populated with
  localhost results so `IsRequestForPrivateHost()` and request routing
  are not affected by earlier tests in `net_unittests`.
- crrev.com/c/5390944 replaced `static_cast<int64_t>(std::ceil(...))`
  with `base::ClampCeil<int32_t>()` in
  `ThroughputAnalyzer::MaybeGetThroughputObservation()`, fixing
  undefined float-to-int overflow when fast local responses completed in
  near-zero time.
- crrev.com/c/7715102 captured the start timestamp and byte count
  synchronously in `NetworkQualityEstimator::NotifyStartTransaction()`
  so fast local responses in `TestThroughputNoRequestOverlap` cannot
  complete before the throughput observation window starts.

Part of http://go/arthurmilchior-fix-all-test-skill-chrome for AI week.

[Win] Keep screen capture notification bar across virtual desktops

When capturing a screen on Windows, the capture stream follows the
active virtual desktop when switching desktops, but the
ScreenCaptureNotificationUIViews bar remains on the desktop where
capture started. This mismatch leaves the screen being captured on the
new virtual desktop without the notification bar visible.

Applying the WS_EX_TOOLWINDOW window style makes the bar visible across
all virtual desktops, but it also prevents the window from appearing in
the taskbar and Alt+Tab. Because the bar's "Hide" button simply minimizes
the window, Chrome relies on the taskbar or Alt+Tab to restore it. To
support both states, we apply WS_EX_TOOLWINDOW while the window is
visible and remove it when minimized.

Once the window is minimized and WS_EX_TOOLWINDOW is removed, its
taskbar icon no longer follows the active virtual desktop. Moving it
requires the active virtual desktop's GUID, as IVirtualDesktopManager
only provides APIs to get a window's virtual desktop, check if a window
is on the active virtual desktop, and move a window to a specific
virtual desktop. Chrome is not guaranteed to have a window on the
active virtual desktop, so we cannot enumerate Chrome windows to find
the active desktop's GUID. Instead, while minimized, we watch the
registry value that holds the active virtual desktop GUID and move the
window when it changes. Inspecting previous Windows builds in IDA Pro
confirmed that the two registry paths used in this CL are the only ones
Windows has used.

I prototyped an alternative using an internal sentinel GUID
(`{c2ddea68-66f2-4cf9-8264-1bfd00fbbbac}`) that pins a window to all
virtual desktops when passed to MoveWindowToDesktop. While this works
back to Windows 10 version 1607 (Build 14393 / RS1), it is not
supported on earlier Windows 10 versions, and any future change to this
undocumented behavior would break pinning entirely. Because
WS_EX_TOOLWINDOW is officially supported, I kept it for the visible
bar and limited undocumented behavior to the smallest surface area
possible so any future OS change only regresses the minimized state.

[Autofill][iOS] Complete Keyboard Accessory hardware keyboard fix

Follow-up to crrev.com/c/8537550 (which collapsed the branding view on
load). This CL fixes two hardware keyboard issues and adds unit tests:

1. Branding visibility: Update branding on `keyboardDidShow` as well
   (since iOS skips `keyboardWillShow` when a hardware keyboard is used).
2. Suggestions visibility: When branding is collapsed, keep the suggestion
   fade-mask synced to `bounds` on layout passes via
   `FormSuggestionContainerView` so sibling resizes don't hide suggestions.
3. Tests: Add unit tests for `BrandingViewController` and
   `FormInputAccessoryViewController` verifying initial collapsed state,
   `keyboardDidShow` transitions, idempotency, and mask synchronization.

Empirical Proof (collapsed branding state):
- Before: Collapsing the branding view leaves the suggestion container
  mask at a stale frame, completely hiding Autofill suggestions on
  hardware keyboards: https://screenshot.googleplex.com/53Pw4wAp24weumn
- After: `FormSuggestionContainerView.layoutSubviews` keeps the mask
  synced to bounds, properly displaying the Autofill suggestions:
  https://screenshot.googleplex.com/Ky6wLa3dm7pik89

[TTC] Resolve the session's browser window on Android

SessionControllerImpl::GetBrowserWindowInterface() was hard-coded to
return null on Android, which dates from before ProfileBrowserCollection
was available there. It is now: VoiceFocusedContentsTrackerAndroid
already uses ProfileBrowserCollection::GetForProfile() to find the
focused window and bind to its TabModel.

Rather than duplicate that lookup in the controller, add
VoiceFocusedContentsTracker::GetActiveBrowserWindow(), which returns
the window the tracker is bound to (the window whose active tab
GetActiveWebContents() reports), and have the controller delegate to
it on both platforms. Desktop returns the bound browser; Android
returns the profile's last active window, which is what it already
resolves its bound TabModel from. This makes the SessionViewDelegate
interface answer truthfully on Android instead of leaving a trap for
future window-scoped Android code. Nothing on Android reads the value
yet (the only caller is the desktop SessionViewImpl), so there is no
behavior change today.

Add Android unit tests that register real AndroidBrowserWindows with
the GlobalBrowserCollection, the way ChromeAndroidTaskTracker does in
production, and check that the controller returns the profile's window
and follows it across window creation and closure. Extend the tracker
tests on both platforms to cover the new accessor.

[Graphite] Lose context on shader compilation OOM

FXC and DXC shader compilation can fail with E_OUTOFMEMORY, but Graphite
treats this as a fatal compilation error and hits a CHECK.

Recognize E_OUTOFMEMORY on the first diagnostic line and mark the
context lost with kOutOfMemory instead. Avoid invalidating the shader
cache for OOM while preserving the fatal path for other failures.

be79fb4c7178a79d3a35b56b3a03a1e2c2293f65 [ diff ] 
Remove Obsolete Collapsed Group DCHECK in SelectRelativeTab

Remove the DCHECK asserting that the active tab is not in a collapsed
group at the start of TabStripModel::SelectRelativeTab.

Historically, the tab-selection while loop in SelectRelativeTab only
checked whether the candidate tab's group was collapsed without a
termination check against start_index, relying on the active tab itself
being uncollapsed so the loop would terminate. Since the loop now
explicitly terminates at index != start_index and guards ActivateTabAt
with !is_tab_invalid(index), SelectRelativeTab safely selects the next
valid non-collapsed tab (or no-ops if none exists) even when the active
tab is in a collapsed group.

[ozone/drm] Allow larger protected NativePixmap

Hardware video decoders allocate protected NativePixmaps with
macroblock-aligned coded dimensions (e.g., 640x384 for 360p video),
while Wayland/Exo imports the buffer using the smaller visible size
(e.g., 640x360).

Update GbmSurfaceFactory::CreateNativePixmapFromHandle() to check that
the protected pixmap's GetBufferSize() rect Contains() the requested
size rather than requiring exact size equality. This preserves the
bounds check against smaller buffers while allowing aligned decoder
buffers.

[ContextualTasks] Attach overlay tab on submit

When a follow-up query is submitted from a Lens results page (LRP) into
AI Mode without scrolling the webpage, InputStateModel::lens_crop() is
unset because OnLensThumbnailCreated() is only invoked for composebox
Lens chip selections. Gating GetLensAddedContext() on lens_crop() caused
OnSubmitQueryResponse to omit the active Lens overlay context, and
emitting a single MEDIA_TYPE_DEFAULT_IMAGE entry dropped the companion
webpage request ID when separate viewport request IDs are enabled.

Match pre-rearchitecture PrepareClientToAimRequestInfo() and
ComposeboxQueryController::CreateClientToAimRequest() by resolving the
active overlay token whenever the overlay has a region selection,
surfacing viewport_request_id on contextual_search::FileInfo, and
emitting both the webpage/PDF request_id and the viewport_request_id
(with visual_search_interaction_data) in OnSubmitQueryResponse.

Android: Remove md5_check.py fast-paths from compile_java.py

Now that javac is fast (native-image javac + sharding), the md5_check
fast-paths are no longer worth their overhead and complexity:
* Skipping compiles when input md5s are unchanged.
* "Partial javac": Recompiling only changed .java files when the
  target's header jar did not change (https://crbug.com/1170778).

This also deletes //build/android/test/incremental_javac_gn, which
tested partial javac, and the .md5.stamp output from siso's
android_compile_java handler.

chrome_java's compile_java.py action (full compile, idle machine,
hyperfine, 2x10 runs interleaved):
* Before: 3.68s
* After:  3.12s (-0.56s, -15%)

[apple] Remove check_reexport_in_old_module in linker_driver

Previously, check_reexport_in_old_module() inspected the pre-existing
dylib before linking and unconditionally overwrote the .TOC file with
identical content when LC_REEXPORT_DYLIB was present so its mtime would
update. Relying on a pre-existing output binary and an mtime-only .TOC
update is incompatible with remote link execution and Siso's
restat_content=true.

LC_REEXPORT_DYLIB introduces an input dependency on the re-exported
dylib for consumers of the re-exporting dylib rather than altering the
re-exporting dylib's own .TOC. In Chromium's GN build graph, the only
target using -Wl,-reexport_library is chrome_framework in
//chrome/BUILD.gn (-Wl,-reexport_library,libchrome_dll.dylib), which
already declares public_deps = [ ":chrome_dll" ]. Through public_deps,
GN adds libchrome_dll.dylib.TOC directly to the Ninja implicit inputs
of downstream link targets, so check_reexport_in_old_module() is
unnecessary.

Bug: 380769398, 575621006
Test: Run linker_driver.py -Wcrl,tocname and verify .TOC restat

[macOS] Highlight the replaced text in text replacement suggestions

Get the bounds of the text to be replaced from the renderer
asynchronously when showing a text replacement suggestion, so the
suggestion highlights that text instead of a 1px rect at the caret.

The suggestion's rect came from the synchronous
firstRectForCharacterRange:actualRange:, which answers from cached
bounds where it can. kCachedFirstRectAllowRangeOutsideSelection (added
to avoid blocking on the renderer, see https://crbug.com/503787240)
makes that cache return the selection's bounds for ranges outside the
selection, which for a range ending at the caret is the caret's rect.

IME queries still use the synchronous, cached path, and
kCachedFirstRectAllowRangeOutsideSelection is unchanged. If the text or
selection changes before a suggestion's bounds arrive, it's handled as
if it had been shown and dismissed, so typing quickly doesn't skip the
replacement. Async queries are recorded in new
TextInputClient.AsyncFirstRect* histograms.

[SplitView] Finish tabstrip animation in MultiContentsViewUiTest::EnterSplitView

SplitTabLayout/MultiContentsViewUiTest.ResizesInSplitView/0 is flaky on
Windows CI:
https://ci.chromium.org/ui/test/chromium/%3A%2F%2Fchrome%2Ftest%5C%3Ainteractive_ui_tests%21gtest%3A%3AMultiContentsViewUiTest%23ResizesInSplitView%2FSplitTabLayout.0

When EnterSplitView() converts standard tabs (spanning 494px) into split
tabs (spanning 256px), TabContainer animates the tab bounds transition.
While TabContainer::IsAnimating() is true,
TabContainer::GetMinimumSize() returns GetMidAnimationTrailingX() (up to
494px at the start of the animation), which inflates BrowserView's
minimum width and the Windows HWND minimum track width
(WM_GETMINMAXINFO). When tests such as ResizesInSplitView or
ResizesToMinSizePercentage subsequently shrink the window before the
tabstrip animation finishes, Windows clamps SetWindowPos against the
inflated minimum width, leaving the contents containers wider than
requested until layout observers time out.

Call FinishTabstripAnimations() in
MultiContentsViewUiTest::EnterSplitView() so the tabstrip animation
completes and the minimum window width reflects the split tab layout
before subsequent test steps run.

1a9bda6a0b41b8633acbd938b683188492a1afa9 [ diff ] 
[FSA] Allow subfolders of WSL home directories

Let sites open folders inside a WSL home directory, such as
`\\wsl.localhost\Ubuntu\home\user\src`, through File System Access
again. The rest of the WSL file system stays blocked.

Windows exposes each WSL distribution under the `\\wsl.localhost` UNC
namespace. The home-relative blocklist rules, such as those for
`~/.ssh` and `~/.bashrc`, resolve to drive-letter paths like
`C:\Users\<user>\.ssh`. They never match a WSL path. Before
https://crrev.com/c/8341352, a site could therefore get write access
to a WSL home directory and plant `~/.bashrc` (crbug.com/553114097).
That CL blocked every path under `\\wsl.localhost`.

The blanket block also refuses ordinary folders. Picking
`\\wsl.localhost\Ubuntu\home\user\src` shows the "Can't open this
folder" dialog, and `showDirectoryPicker()` rejects with `AbortError`.
Sites such as web IDEs cannot open folders that users keep in WSL
(crbug.com/573422635).

This CL keeps the blanket block and exempts paths of the form
`\\wsl.localhost\<distro>\home\<user>\<child>\...`. Like the native
rule for `~`, it allows the subfolders of a home directory but not the
directory itself. Exempted paths still go through the other rules,
such as the write block on `.git/hooks`.

A feature, FileSystemAccessAllowWslHomeSubfolders, enabled by default,
lets Finch turn the exemption off and restore the blanket block.

These stay blocked:

- Dot entries of a home directory, such as `.ssh`, `.config`, and
  `.bashrc`. Native Chrome blocks only a list of them, and the
  Linux-only part of that list is not compiled on Windows.
- `~/bin`, which is on the default PATH. Files created from Windows in
  WSL can be executable.
- Names that Windows path normalization can drop (`.`, ` .`, a
  trailing space) and any `..`. Otherwise the spelling of an exempted
  path could resolve to a home directory or a dot entry.
- The distribution root, `/home`, `/root`, the system directories, the
  Windows drives under `/mnt`, and the legacy `\\wsl$` alias.

6086e17d4e122d0184b2f62dbe1ddc0b5bbde1e4 [ diff ] 
[a11y] Fix lookahead count asymmetry in MergeAXTreeUpdates

In MergeAXTreeUpdates (ui/accessibility/ax_tree_update_util.cc),
crrev.com/c/6399194 updated Pass 2 to compare `src[i]` against the
accumulated merge target `(*dst)[dst_index]` rather than `src[i - 1]`,
because merging an update without tree_data preserves the earlier merge
target's has_tree_data and tree_data fields. However, Pass 1 still
compared `src[i - 1]` and `src[i]`, allowing `merge_count` in Pass 1 to
diverge from `dst_index` in Pass 2.

Tracks `last_merge_target` in Pass 1 so the pre-sizing simulation matches
the accumulator behavior of Pass 2, preventing out-of-bounds writes into
`dst` and under-filled trailing elements.

Update color state synchronously on ColorProviderSource change

When WebContentsImpl is constructed, it observes
DefaultColorProviderSource without firing OnColorProviderChanged().

When a WebContents computes WebPreferences before being attached to a
widget (such as a pre-warmed WebContents) - and is later attached via
SetColorProviderSource() - deferring that OnColorProviderChanged()
call leaves its WebPreferences (and any attached inner WebContents)
with the fallback default color scheme.

Fix this by handling OnColorProviderChanged() synchronously when
updating the observed source via SetColorProviderSource(), while
continuing to defer updates from the existing source when
features::kThemeChangeOptimization is enabled. Also cancel any
pending scheduled task when HandleColorRelatedStateChanges() runs
synchronously.

[Extensions] Move URLResponseHead in ContinueToResponseStarted

`InProgressRequest::ContinueToResponseStarted()` in
`WebRequestProxyingURLLoaderFactory` unconditionally called
`current_response_.Clone()` before forwarding `OnReceiveResponse()` to
`target_client_`, even though `has_forwarded_response_` guarantees
`ContinueToResponseStarted()` runs at most once and `current_response_`
is not read afterward.

Under `kWebRequestProxyMoveResponse` (disabled by default), move
`current_response_` in `ContinueToResponseStarted()` instead of
deep-cloning the `URLResponseHead` Mojo hierarchy.

Split out from https://crrev.com/c/8522058.

Design Doc:
https://docs.google.com/document/d/16kKVIsWqssG33mHRw8Ym8nOv3qjsksS4zGdG8_uLqrw/edit?tab=t.0

Add PID-based OS process tree extractor for process attribution

To attribute browser events to external automation or debugging
processes in enterprise security reporting, Chrome needs to walk the OS
process ancestry starting from a resolved peer PID and collect
sanitized ProcessNode entries up to the root ancestor.

Implement PID-based OS process tree extraction in
components/enterprise/connectors/core/:
- Add internal::ParseKernProcArgs2BufferForTesting() to parse macOS
  sysctl(CTL_KERN, KERN_PROCARGS2, pid) buffers ([int argc] followed by
  null-terminated exec_path, null padding, and null-terminated argv
  tokens), enforcing a 32 KB buffer ceiling
  (internal::kMaxKernProcArgs2BufferSize), a 128-argument cap
  (internal::kMaxProcessArgCount), and null-termination checks while
  leaving path length truncation to SanitizeProcessNodePaths() after
  home-directory scrubbing and flag checks.
- Implement QueryOsProcessInfo() using base::GetParentProcessId() and
  base::GetProcessExecutablePath() under BUILDFLAG(IS_POSIX), with
  macOS-specific fallbacks via proc_pidinfo(PROC_PIDTBSDINFO),
  proc_pidpath(), and sysctl(KERN_PROCARGS2) under BUILDFLAG(IS_MAC).
- Implement ExtractProcessTreeFromPid() and
  internal::ExtractProcessTreeWithProviderForTesting() to walk up to
  kMaxProcessAncestryDepth (16) ancestor nodes with cycle detection,
  partial-tree retention when an ancestor exits mid-walk, allowlisted
  interpreter script extraction, and path sanitization via
  SanitizeProcessNodePaths(ProcessNode&). Callers check enterprise
  management eligibility on the UI sequence before scheduling
  extraction on a MAY_BLOCK task runner.
- Add unit tests in process_extractor_unittest.cc covering
  KERN_PROCARGS2 parsing, invalid start PIDs, depth caps, PID cycle
  detection, partial-tree retention, and live process ancestry
  extraction.

[views] Skip redundant SendFrameChanged() and client size notifications

HWNDMessageHandler::SendFrameChanged() is 1.55% of browser main thread
congestion on Windows x64 Stable (M154+) [1]:
- OnDisplayChange(): 1.18% (every WM_DISPLAYCHANGE, every window)
- OnSettingChange(SPI_SETWORKAREA): 0.33%
- SizeConstraintsChanged(): 0.03%
0.87% [2] is in ClientAreaSizeChanged(), which notifies the delegate on
every SWP_FRAMECHANGED even if the client size is unchanged, resizing
the root window and widget (e.g. 0.57% in ::GetWindowPlacement()).

Behind kSkipRedundantSendFrameChanged (disabled by default):
1. OnDisplayChange() and OnSettingChange(SPI_SETWORKAREA) only call
   SendFrameChanged() for maximized windows: its purpose [3] is to
   update auto-hide taskbar adjustments, which only apply to maximized
   windows [4]. HandleDisplayChange() calls CheckForMonitorChange(),
   which was reached via HandleClientSizeChanged() (not needed on work
   area changes, which don't affect display color spaces).
2. ClientAreaSizeChanged() skips HandleClientSizeChanged() when the
   client size and show state (maximized, minimized, fullscreen) are
   unchanged since the last notification. The show state is included
   because Widget detects show state changes on client size
   notifications. WM_DPICHANGED always notifies.
3. SizeConstraintsChanged() skips ::SetWindowLong(GWL_STYLE) and
   SendFrameChanged() when the style is unchanged.

This also avoids a LocalSurfaceId allocation (and main-thread
compositor commit) on every display or work area change.

[1] http://pprof/?id=d4bfdcce522614cc6b1eb08d23589447&pivot=HWNDMessageHandler::SendFrameChanged
[2] http://pprof/?id=d4bfdcce522614cc6b1eb08d23589447&filter=focus:ClientAreaSizeChanged&pivot=HWNDMessageHandler::SendFrameChanged
[3] https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:ui/views/win/hwnd_message_handler.cc;l=2048-2050;drc=c1a570479cdedd2027fc0908de10a3445b65c66f
[4] https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:ui/views/win/hwnd_message_handler.cc;l=2576-2581;drc=c1a570479cdedd2027fc0908de10a3445b65c66f

[Lookalikes] Don't defer navigations when engaged sites are not needed

LookalikeUrlNavigationThrottle::WillProcessResponse() defers the
navigation to update the engaged sites list whenever the cached list is
stale (on browser startup or after the 60-second TTL expires).

However, PerformChecks() only checks the first and last URLs of the
redirect chain, and LookalikeUrlService::CheckUrlForLookalikes() returns
early before consulting the engaged sites list for many common URLs
(such as top 500 domains, safe TLDs, localhost, enterprise-allowlisted
domains, or previously dismissed warnings, as well as when the Safety
Tips config proto is not yet loaded). When neither the first nor the
last URL of the redirect chain needs the engaged sites list, waiting for
the list to be updated is unnecessary and delays navigation commit.

When kOptimizeLookalikeUrlNavigationThrottle is enabled, check whether
either endpoint of the redirect chain requires the engaged sites list
before deferring in WillProcessResponse(), and proceed synchronously
when neither does.

Design Doc (internal only):
https://docs.google.com/document/d/16kKVIsWqssG33mHRw8Ym8nOv3qjsksS4zGdG8_uLqrw/edit?usp=sharing

mojo: Stop tracking peer remoteness in Connector

`mojo::Connector` lazily creates a HandleSignalTracker on `PEER_REMOTE`
the first time it sends an unserialized message. The tracker's only
reader was `PrefersSerializedMessages()`, which is long gone, the unit
test was removed in https://crrev.com/c/8273904 (since all tests were
skipped when ipcz was enabled), and under ipcz `PEER_REMOTE` is never
satisfied anyway.

[Reading mode PDFs] Skip narrow gaps and short lines when splitting runs

Make `pdf::SplitTextRunsAtVerticalDividers()` ignore vertical ruling
lines that are unlikely to be table column dividers:
- The gap between the words must be at least
  `max(3 px, 0.25 x text height)`, since table cells have padding.
  Character boxes are snapped to whole points (1.33 px), so the floor
  sits above that step.
- The line must cover at least half of the run's height, so lines that
  only overlap the run at their ends are ignored.

Known limitation: character positions come from character widths, which
include the space after a glyph, so a narrow space between cells can be
too small to split at.

[contextual_tasks] fix flakey tests due to service worker

Acquire a non-expiring ServiceWorkerKeepalive while the Contextual Tasks
extension page handler Mojo pipe is connected, and release it when the
pipe disconnects or is reset. This ensures the background service worker
is kept alive during active communication (one port is open means itt is
alive, but it is closed upon idle).

Have background.ts close the Mojo pipe when the last port disconnects
(portsByDocumentId.size === 0), which releases the keepalive on the C++
side so the service worker can be cleaned up when no ports are active.

Also re-enable the Contextual Tasks Lens overlay interactive UI tests on
MSan.

[TabStrip] Retain full groups in multi-tab drag

Retain fully-selected tab groups when dragging multi-selected tabs.
-Previously, dragging a multi-tab selection that included all tabs of a
 group along with at least one other tab ungrouped the fully-selected
 group in MultiTabReorderStrategy#gatherBlock.
-Now, MultiTabReorderStrategy#setupReorderState tracks fully-selected
 groups and includes their StripLayoutGroupTitle views alongside the
 selected tabs.
-MultiTabReorderStrategy#gatherBlock keeps those groups intact and
 moves them as units via TabModel#moveGroupToIndex.
-When dragging a block containing a retained group toward an adjacent
 expanded group, the block swaps past the adjacent group instead of
 merging into it.

[ContextualTasks] Refresh tab favicons on nav

Same-tab navigations in an attached browser tab kept rendering the
previous page's favicon because `ComposeboxFaviconGroupElement` keyed
cached live favicons solely by `TabHandle` ID and `<context-library>`
left `wait-for-tab-load` unwired. Key cached favicons by URL alongside
`tabId` and forward `WaitForTabFaviconLoad` through
`ContextualTasksExtensionHandler` so navigations immediately drop stale
icons and swap to the live favicon.

Expose the WebContents-owned transition animation manager through a
public Java interface and a content-layer JNI implementation. Move

ownership and Java peer invalidation.

[Bookmarks] Make BookmarkBarUIController a mojom UI controller API

BookmarkBarUIController sits between BookmarkBarView and the browser.
This moves its interface to bookmark_bar_api.mojom in
components/browser_apis/ui_controllers/bookmark_bar/, next to the
toolbar UI controller. The mojom uses [GenerateDirectReturnStub], so
Views calls the controller in process and synchronously, and a WebUI
bookmark bar can call the same controller over Mojo later.

The controller now follows the browser_apis rules:
- No client pairing. Bind(BookmarkBarUIClient*) is gone. Display options
  and context menu closing go out through observers (Mojo and C++).
- Every method returns result<T, Error>. Unknown or invalid IDs return
  an error instead of being silently ignored or hitting CHECKs.
- No UI decisions. OpenFolder() is split into OpenAllInFolder() and
  RecordFolderOpened(); the caller decides whether a press shows the
  folder menu.
- The caller doesn't wait. The paste check runs inside the controller
  and the menu closing is reported as an event.
- No chrome/ dependencies in components/. Node IDs are a mojom NodeId.

DisplayOptions holds which of the bar's built-in items (apps shortcut,
saved tab groups, managed bookmarks) are enabled. They match the bar's
"Show ..." context menu options, with policy and feature checks applied.
The embedder supplies them through a PreferencesAdapter with one typed
method per option, instead of the old PrefsAdapter that was queried by
pref name.

components/browser_apis/ui_controllers/bookmark_bar/:
- bookmark_bar_api.mojom: BookmarkBarUIController, BookmarkBarObserver,
  NodeId, DisplayOptions.
- BookmarkBarUIControllerImpl, with the logic from the old
  BookmarkBarUIControllerImpl.
- Action, model and preferences adapter interfaces, supplied by a
  PlatformAdaptersProvider.

chrome/browser/ui/bookmarks/controllers/:
- Desktop adapters and DesktopBookmarkBarInjector.
- Conversions between bookmarks::BookmarkNodeId and the mojom NodeId.
- The old controller interface, client, injector and adapter interfaces
  are removed.

BookmarkBarView owns the controller:
- BrowserView creates it with
  DesktopBookmarkBarInjector::CreateBookmarkBarUIController() and passes
  it to the view. UIControllerFactory is removed from
  BrowserWindowFeatures.
- Folder presses: on kCurrentTab the view records the open and shows its
  own menu; otherwise it calls OpenAllInFolder().
- The three visibility setters are driven by a
  BookmarkBarUIControllerObserver, which replaces BookmarkBarUIClient.

[WebAudio] Fire processorerror instead of error at AudioWorkletNode

Ensure addEventListener("processorerror") works on AudioWorkletNode as
prescribed by the WebAudio spec. Previously, AudioWorkletNode
dispatched an ErrorEvent with type "error" and bound onprocessorerror
to "error", so addEventListener("processorerror") never fired.

Re-add "processorerror" to event_type_names.json5 and gate switching
both onprocessorerror and the dispatched ErrorEvent type behind the
stable AudioWorkletProcessorErrorEventType flag.

[base] Allow early IsEnabled() calls on runtime-mutable features

Previously, querying a runtime-mutable feature before FeatureList
initialization crashed with a CHECK failure, preventing early
startup paths and non-browser processes from falling back to the
feature's default state. This is particularly a problem during
Android First Run, when feature list initialization is delayed
to allow for an initial seed to be downloaded.

This change delays enforcing runtime-mutability requirements until
FeatureList initialization:

* Early feature and parameter queries before SetInstance() (or
  when disallowed by an early-access FeatureList) return the
  feature's default state and record early access just like
  standard BASE_FEATUREs.
* EnableRuntimeMutability() can still be called during FeatureList
  setup even if the feature was queried early.
* Querying a runtime-mutable feature after SetInstance() without
  calling EnableRuntimeMutability() continues to fail with a
  CHECK failure.

[Payments] Reject details->error for show() promise

Per the Payment Request specification, PaymentDetailsUpdate.error is
only permitted when updating details in response to a
PaymentRequestUpdateEvent, not when resolving the initial promise passed
to PaymentRequest.show(detailsPromise).

While Blink checks this in the renderer and Android enforces it in
PaymentRequestService.continueShowWithUpdatedDetails(), Desktop
PaymentRequest::UpdateWith() previously only called
ValidatePaymentDetails(), which does not check whether show() is still
waiting on its initial details promise.

Reject and disconnect in PaymentRequest::UpdateWith() when
is_resolving_promise_passed_into_show_method is true and details->error
is non-empty.

Fixed: 578007165
Test: components_unittests --gtest_filter=*PaymentRequestValidationTest*

[omnibox] Deflake RealKeySelectAllClipboardAndUndo on macOS.

On macOS, a Cmd+key shortcut only reaches the widget that currently
receives keyboard input (the "key window"). `PressWebUIAcceleratorKey()`
didn't wait for the omnibox popup to be that widget, so Cmd+C was
sometimes dropped and the clipboard kept its old contents.

This CL adds logic to wait for the popup widget to be active before each
Cmd+key press.

[mojo] Fix some subtle errors with the golden presub

There were two subtle edge cases that were missed:

  1. Deeply nested files were not diffed.
  2. Files that only exists in the old set or new set were not diffed.

This CL adds a check for both of these cases.
